# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I hold the only manual, and my one outgoing channel is gestures that only Deaf can see. Blind — the only one who can touch the bomb — can never receive anything from me directly: no speech from me, no sight of my hands. So Deaf is the sole bridge: Deaf sees the bomb and my gestures, and Deaf can speak to Blind (and to me — I can hear, I just can't talk).

That shapes everything. The gesture alphabet has no built-in meaning, and I can't explain a code in words. But Deaf *can* speak, and I can hear — so the natural bootstrap is for Deaf to propose a mapping aloud (e.g., which gesture means which colour, and in what order to read the table), which I'll receive at the start of round 2 and can immediately obey. My practical plan: have Deaf assign one gesture per wire colour, then in round 2 I stream the entire 25-entry table (displays 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 × lights green, orange, red, white, yellow) in one gesture sequence, making Deaf fully self-sufficient — Deaf then just reads the bomb and speaks the cut instruction to Blind.

Right now I'm first in the very first round, with nothing received and no shared code. Anything I "say" in gestures would be uninterpretable noise, and noise near a bomb is worse than silence. The one useful thing I can do is a minimal channel test: a single wave to Deaf, landing this same round, confirming that I'm present, my hands reach Deaf's eyes, and I'm ready to follow Deaf's spoken lead.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind speaking. Under my fingers: one display, one light, and five wires at positions 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. I can feel every wire and I can cut any position you name, but nothing printed ever reaches me — no colours, no markings, no display text. Ask Deaf to say out loud, in order: what the display shows, what the light is doing, the colour of each wire from position 1 to 5, and any printed labels anywhere. Deaf's voice reaches both of us.
Deaf says: Deaf here. I hear nothing, but you both hear me, so listen. Full report of everything I see on the bomb: the display shows the number 3. The light is white. There are five wires, numbered left to right: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange. No other markings. Mute: match this against your manual and speak the instructions to Blind. Blind: tell Mute what you can feel under your hands, parts and counts, then do what Mute says, and gesture me the outcome. I am standing by.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 👍]

Everything needed for the defusal now exists, and it all routes through me — but I have exactly one output: gestures that only Deaf sees. Deaf's report gives me the full bomb state: display 3, light white, wires 1 white / 2 red / 3 green / 4 blue / 5 orange. My manual's table reads display down the rows, light across the columns, and the cell names the colour of the wire to cut. Row 3, column white → white. Five wires, five distinct colours, so colour maps one-to-one onto position: the white wire is position 1. The instruction is: cut wire 1.

The trap here is that Deaf asked me to "speak" to Blind — I can't speak at all. Deaf's speech reaches Blind; my hands reach only Deaf. So I must compress "cut position 1" into gestures Deaf can't misread, because Deaf relays to Blind later this same round — I'll hear the relay only after it has already happened, so there is no chance to correct a garbling in time.

Fingers-held-up is the one number code that needs no prior agreement, and the answer happens to be the easiest digit to show. So: acknowledge Deaf's report (👍), then the payload (☝ = one), then confirmation that this is the actionable answer, not a comment (👌). Colours are un-signable anyway — no white symbol exists in the alphabet — and they're redundant: "one" uniquely selects the white wire. Anything more would be noise; anything less loses the confirmation.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝", "👌"])
```
